topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing and introduces the challenge of complement terminology.

topics.label: Fundamentals and core architecture of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts, nomenclature rules, and the central role of C3 in complement function.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct recognition pathways that generate convertases to reach the complement activation threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream processes by which activated complement eliminates pathogens through opsonization, inflammation, and direct lysis.

topics.label: Host cell regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the regulatory mechanisms that protect host tissues from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the diverse clinical disease presentations resulting from genetic or acquired deficiencies across the complement pathway.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion mechanisms and applications of protein A
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how pathogens counteract complement attack and how these bacterial evasion tools are utilized in medicine and research.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic wraps up the lecture on complement and previews the upcoming session on adaptive immunity.
